name: Shiratani Unsuikyo (白谷雲水峡)
why: A ravine of clear pools and old cedars, through a forest where every rock and root is green with moss, up to a granite rock over the island's peaks.
book: No permit. A forest donation (500 yen when last published) is collected at the entrance building. Bus from Miyanoura port, about 35 minutes, or by car. Put a climbing registration form in the box at the start; the forest may close under a severe weather warning.
water: Streams along the way and a toilet at Shiratani hut; nothing to buy above the entrance. Carry 1 litre.
dangers: Wet granite and roots: the trail is slippery all year.
Several stream crossings on stones: after heavy rain they can be impassable, wait or turn back.
Taikoiwa is a bare rock with a drop: stay back from the edge in wind.
turnaround: If the streams are over the stepping stones, go back to the entrance.

points.name: Shiratani ravine entrance
points.note: About 620 m, by the bus stop and the administration building. The trail crosses the Satsuki suspension bridge over the ravine.

points.name: Moss forest (Kokemusu-mori)
points.note: Just above Shiratani hut: the moss-covered forest that is the reason most people come.

points.name: Tsujitoge pass
points.note: The pass on the ridge; Taikoiwa is a short, steep climb to the left.

points.name: Taikoiwa rock
points.note: About 1,050 m: a granite slab over the Anbo valley with Yakushima's central peaks in front. Back the same way.
